newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: HORSE RACING-IMPERIAL CALL FACES STIFF OPPOSITION IN HENNESSY.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-IMPERIAL CALL FACES STIFF OPPOSITION IN HENNESSY.

text.p: Ireland's Cheltenham Gold Cup hero, Imperial Call, heads a star-studded field for Sunday's Grade One Hennessy Gold Cup at Leopardstown.
Imperial Call (5-4 favourite) faces seven rivals, three trained in Britain, including 1993 Cheltenham Gold Cup winner, Jodami, in the three mile (4.8-km) contest.

Imperial Call, a faller on his seasonal bow at Punchestown, came to prominence with a victory in last year's Hennessy. "He's in super form, but I would love to see a drop of rain," trainer Fergie Sutherland said.
The official Leopardstown going on Friday was described as good, but the forecast is for showers.
Jodami, winner of three successive Hennessy Gold Cups starting in 1993, was denied the chance to bid for a four-timer by an 11th hour setback 12 months ago. He is 11-2 in the betting for Sunday.

The Grey Monk, trained by Gordon Richards, heads the British challenge at 7-2 while Belmont King, also from England, is quoted at 10-1. British-trained horses have won the race eight times in its 10-year history.
Ireland's latest big-race hope, Danoli, a faller on two of his five starts over fences this season and Jim Dreaper-trained Merry Gale are both quoted at 8-1.
County Limerick-based handler Michael Hourigan has elected to run Dorans Pride in the Grade Two Scalp Chase, over two miles and five furlongs (4.2-km), rather than in the Hennessy.
"I had a word with (owner) Tom Doran and with so many good horses likely to run in the Hennessy we have decided to keep our fellow in the novice ranks," Hourigan said.
"Dorans Pride is well and we will just hope for another win in the Scalp Chase before making up our minds about his Cheltenham target."
Top prospect Istabraq runs in a novice hurdle as a warm-up race for one of the big events at Cheltenham.
